themes_detail.label: Street Trees Dying or Damaged
themes_detail.summary: Damaged Tree complaints spiked to 9 last week—a 1700% increase vs. 0.5 weekly average over prior 8 weeks—suggesting a sudden environmental or weather event affecting the district's canopy this week.
evidence: 9 Damaged Tree complaints last week vs. 0.5 weekly average over 8 weeks (z-score: 12.02)
1700% spike represents most statistically anomalous single-category surge in district data
No prior pattern of tree damage complaints suggests acute trigger (storm, disease, or maintenance failure)
reporting_angles: Was there a weather event or infrastructure failure that damaged trees across Highbridge/Concourse this past week?
Interview Parks Department and residents about what trees are dying and why; map locations of complaints

themes_detail.label: Garbage Collection Failing
themes_detail.summary: Missed Collection complaints jumped to 11 last week—a 1157% spike vs. 0.9 weekly average—indicating a sudden sanitation service breakdown in the district this week.
evidence: 11 Missed Collection complaints last week vs. 0.9 weekly average over 8 weeks (z-score: 10.92)
Second-highest spike after Damaged Trees, suggesting systemic service failure rather than isolated incidents
Aligns with historical community board budget request for sewer/sanitation infrastructure upgrades
reporting_angles: Did Sanitation Services experience staffing shortages, vehicle breakdown, or route changes last week?
Interview affected residents and Sanitation Department to identify which blocks or routes were affected

themes_detail.label: Police and Emergency Response Surge
themes_detail.summary: Emergency Response Team complaints jumped to 3 last week—a 2300% spike vs. 0.1 weekly average—alongside a 142% jump in Non-Emergency Police Matter complaints (13 vs. 5.4 weekly average), suggesting either escalating street incidents or increased police activity this week.
evidence: 3 Emergency Response Team complaints last week vs. 0.1 weekly average (z-score: 8.69)
13 Non-Emergency Police Matter complaints last week vs. 5.4 weekly average (z-score: 3.05, up 142%)
Dual spike suggests possible crime incident cluster, large police operation, or public order event
reporting_angles: Did a specific crime, accident, or public safety incident trigger the ERT deployment last week?
Contact NYPD and community leaders to identify what prompted the spike in police-related 311 complaints

themes_detail.label: Street Noise Escalation
themes_detail.summary: Street/Sidewalk Noise complaints surged to 138 last week—a 318% increase vs. 33.0 weekly average over 8 weeks—the largest absolute spike among ambient quality-of-life issues, pointing to construction, events, or traffic disruptions this week.
evidence: 138 Street/Sidewalk Noise complaints last week vs. 33.0 weekly average (z-score: 3.49, up 318%)
Largest volume surge among non-heat, non-residential categories, affecting outdoor quality of life
Complements broader pattern of environmental disruptions (trees, collection) suggesting area-wide disturbance this week
reporting_angles: Is there ongoing construction, street work, or a major event generating noise across the district?
Map noise complaints by location and interview residents about what is causing the disruption

themes_detail.label: Lead Exposure Concern (Older Signal)
themes_detail.summary: Lead complaints peaked at 5 three weeks ago—a 300% spike vs. 1.2 weekly average—suggesting housing stock contamination concerns; though the spike is older than this week, it warrants investigation given heat/housing prominence in district and lack of follow-up signal.
evidence: 5 Lead complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 1.2 weekly average (z-score: 3.87, up 300%)
No sustained follow-up complaints in past 2 weeks, but lead exposure is a persistent health hazard in older housing stock
District's high volume of Paint/Plaster and Plumbing complaints (1034 and 1319 respectively) suggests older buildings vulnerable to lead
reporting_angles: Which buildings or blocks triggered the lead spike 3 weeks ago? Have complaints been resolved?
Investigate lead hazards in Highbridge's older housing stock and what enforcement/remediation efforts exist
